narrations.en: Step 33 (Final Step): The visual proof is complete! Starting from the starting condition of directly dividing the numerator by the denominator in a fraction (rational number) to observe whether the numbers after the decimal point end or repeat endlessly, we go through the number theory idea of classifying whether the denominator of the irreducible fraction has only 2 or 5 (can be converted to a fraction raised to the power of 10), or whether there are prime factors other than 2 and 5. When a rational number is expressed as a decimal, the number of non-zero numbers below the decimal point is finite. It was clearly confirmed that the conclusion holds that a finite decimal number or a certain number sequence (cyclic node) becomes a repeating decimal number. The key point to remember here is that not all infinite decimal numbers are irrational numbers! Repeating decimals (e.g. 0.333... = 1/3) are legitimate rational numbers that can be expressed as fractions, while only non-repeating interminating decimals (pi, square root of 2) are irrational. Finally, ask a deeper question. Multiply the repeating decimal x = 0.121212... by 100 to make 100x - x = 99x. How can we convert all repeating decimals to fractions in 1 second?
